events.title: Venezuela Earthquake
events.summary: On 24 June 2026, two strong earthquakes, preliminarily measured at magnitudes 7.1 and 7.5, struck north-central Venezuela in rapid succession, with epicentres near Morón, Carabobo State. The earthquakes were felt across much of the country, including Caracas, La Guaira, Aragua, Carabobo and neighbouring states. Therefore, the national goverment of Venezuela declared the state of emergency.

events.title: Nepal: Rasuwa Flash Flood
events.summary: A major flash flood struck Rasuwa district after a sudden and intense surge in the Bhote Koshi River at approximately 9:15 AM. The flood rapidly impacted the Timure, Rasuwagadhi, and Syabrubesi areas, causing significant damage to settlements, markets, police infrastructure, roads, and hydropower facilities. Authorities have warned that rising water levels could affect downstream communities along the Trishuli River corridor.

events.title: Colombia - Earthquake
events.summary: According to information from the Colombian Geological Service (SGC), an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.4 was recorded on Monday, August 10, 2026, in the morning, with its epicenter in the town of San José del Palmar, in the department of Chocó, located on the Colombian Pacific coast, at a depth of 96 kilometers. Although the epicenter was in the department of Chocó, direct impacts were also felt in the departments of Caldas, Risaralda, and Valle del Cauca.

events.title: Afghanistan: Nuristan Flood
events.summary: On Monday, 20 July 2026, at approximately 3:00 p.m. local time, a sudden flash flood struck the central areas of Nuristan Province following heavy and continuous rainfall. The low-lying areas and communities located along rivers and seasonal watercourses were the most severely affected.

events.title: Panama Earthquake
events.summary: On October 9, 2026, a large earthquake was registered, estimated between 7.2 and 7.7, with an epicenter reported in the area of Tonosí, province of Los Santos. The telluric movement was perceived in much of the national territory and has been followed by various aftershocks, generating structural damage, interruptions of services and preventive evacuations in multiple provinces.

events.title: Liberia: Floods
events.summary: Since August 19, 2026, there has been sustained heavy rainfall consistent with the Liberia rainy season, which has caused widespread flash and riverine flooding across seven counties: Montserrado, Cape Mount, Grand Bassa, Bomi, Bong, Rivergss, and Nimba. Montserrado, home to Monrovia (Liberia's Capital), has a dense urban corridor and the epicenter, with informal settlements along the St. Paul River, StocktonCreek, Du River, and the Mesurado River.

events.title: Philippines: Southwest Monsoon enhanced by Tropical Cyclones Maymay and Dolphin
events.summary: At 8:00 PM on 4 August 2026, the Low-Pressure Area (LPA) located west of Bacnotan, La Union intensified into Tropical Depression MAYMAY, according to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA). By 2:00 AM on 5 August 2026, Tropical Depression MAYMAY further intensified into Tropical Storm MAYMAY (international name: Kujira) while moving slowly near the western coast of Northern Luzon.

events.title: Sierra Leone: Freetown flash flood
events.summary: On the early morning of 3 August 2026, Freetown experienced approximately six to seven hours of continuous heavy rainfall, resulting in widespread flash flooding, severe erosion, and slope collapse incidents across several low-lying and hillside communities. The incidents caused significant damage to homes and infrastructure, displaced hundreds of people, resulted in fatalities and missing persons, and contaminated critical water sources.

events.title: Algeria: Wildfires – July 2026
events.summary: On 18 July 2026, the wildfire emergency in Algeria reached a significant operational peak, with 154 forest, vegetation and agricultural fires recorded within 24 hours across several wilayas. Of these, 138 fires were extinguished, while 16 remained active at the time of reporting.

events.title: Kyrgyzstan: Nooken Mudflow
events.summary: On 13 July 2026 at approximately 19:30 local time, heavy short-duration rainfall in the mountainous areas of Nooken District, Jalal-Abad Oblast triggered mudflows affecting Kochkor-Ata city and surrounding villages. Two mudflow channels overflowed simultaneously: the Besh-Korgon channel inundated residential streets in Kochkor-Ata city and destroyed 3 electricity poles in the Besh-Korgon settlement; the Kara-Bulak channel flooded Ergesh Aliev village.

events.title: Tunisia Wildfires
events.summary: The wave of fires in the Republic of Tunisia began on 1 June 2026, but reached a sharp peak from 12 July 2026 onward, continuing to the time of writing, coinciding with an exceptional heatwave in which temperatures reached close to 50°C in several governorates — including Kairouan, Jendouba, Gabès, Tozeur and Béja — while temperatures in the south-west reached around 49°C due to the hot, dry "Chehili" desert winds, according to the National Institute of Meteorology.

events.title: Tajikistan: Flood and Mudflow Ayni district
events.summary: On 11 July 2026, following intense rainfall, flash floods and mudflows affected the villages of Darg and Kazdon in Shamtuch Jamoat, Ayni District, Sughd Region. Mudflows descended through the Surkhi, Kashak, and Jari river channels, causing significant damage to residential houses, public infrastructure, road networks, water supply systems, agricultural land, and private property. According to the official authorities, no fatalities or injuries have been reported.

events.title: Laos: Flooding Caused by Heavy Rainfall
events.summary: According to the Department of Meteorology and Hydrology (DMH), a tropical depression over the South China Sea is expected to strengthen the south-west monsoon, bringing widespread heavy rainfall, thunderstorms and strong winds across Lao PDR between 2 and 5 July 2026. The forecast indicates an increased risk of flash floods, riverine flooding and landslides, particularly in northern provinces.

events.title: Georgia: Heavy Rain and Floods in Samegrelo and Zemo Svaneti Region
events.summary: On 27 June 2026, continuous heavy rainfall triggered severe flooding in Senaki and Chkhorotsku municipalities in the Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti Region. Heavy rainfall has continued without interruption since the early hours of 27 June, and as of 29 June the emergency situation remains ongoing. Due to the continuing rainfall and flooding, local authorities have not yet been able to complete a comprehensive damage assessment.

events.title: Indonesia - Drought
events.summary: Indonesia is forecasted to experience prolonged dry conditions during the 2026 dry season due to the combined influence of El Niño conditions and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD). According to BMKG, the dry season is expected to begin earlier than normal in many regions, with 57.2% of seasonal zones (ZOM) predicted to experience a longer dry season and 64.5% of Indonesia forecasted to receive below-normal rainfall accumulation during the June–September period.
